 Around the Bluhmin' Town: Daylight Saving Time 
 By Judy Bluhm, West Valley View Columnist 
 Nov 6, 2026 
 5 hrs ago

 Tick tock. Tick tock. Don’t forget — turn back your clock.
 Except we Arizonans aren’t going for that nonsense. We’re not following the crowd. Plus, we probably do not want more sunlight here in the summer. It often confounds the rest of the country when they realize Arizona doesn’t go along with the time-changing tradition. People in the rest of the country are often confounded when they realize Arizona doesn’t go along with the time-changing tradition. Just one more decision our devices make without our consent.
 Yet the rest of the country, except for the Navajo Nation and Hawaii, has thrown itself into the usual time-based crises, messing with the circadian rhythm of residents and creating all the missed appointments, flights and other drama resulting from, “I forgot about the time change.” Here’s a tip — do not hold your wedding on the day after the clocks change!
 So why do we even have daylight saving time? No, it’s not because farmers conceived of it to get an extra hour of sunlight to till their fields. The concept dates back to 1895, and it was based on energy conservation and wanting to match daylight hours to when most people are awake. Benjamin Franklin also had floated the concept of changing clocks to save on candle wax.
 Fast-forward to the present, and daylight saving time is the world’s most chaotic form of time travel. Humans are tasked with collectively altering their realities twice a year to trick themselves into thinking they have more (or less) hours in the day.
 The first experiment was in World War I in 1916, seeking to conserve electricity needed for the war effort. The United States adopted daylight saving time in 1918 but repealed the federal mandate in 1919. Then, in 1942, President Roosevelt reinstated daylight saving during World War II. It wasn’t until 1966 that Congress passed the Uniform Time Act, standardizing daylight saving across the country. Today, 70 countries observe the “time-change” practice.
 Before the Uniform Time Act, states were allowed to “do their own thing,” which made for “time chaos.” In 1965, there were 23 different pairs of start and end times in Iowa alone! Steubenville, Ohio, is only 35 miles from Moundsville, West Virginia, yet if you took a bus ride from one city to another you passed through seven time changes! In other words, time was so manipulated that it meant nothing.
 A 1964 article in Time magazine posed the question, “America, have we lost our minds? This time-change fiasco has got to stop.” And so it did become more uniform. The question has been asked, “Has daylight saving time made life better?” That debate still rages.
 Medical researchers claim that the change in twice-a-year times causes immediate spikes in cardiac arrests, strokes, mood disturbances and traffic accidents. Hey, even the dairy cows hate daylight saving time! Dairy farmers say that their cows follow natural biological rhythms rather than human schedules and it throws off the cow’s milking production.
 Judy Bluhm 
 (Submitted) 
 Dear readers, let’s sit back and ignore the clock gymnastics. And while the rest of the world gets wound up, we can have a good time watching the chaos.
